questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of store management. [2 marks]
(b) State four importance of store management. [8 marks]
(c) State five qualities of a good store manager. [5 marks]
(d) Distinguish between pre-sale and after-sale services, giving one example of each. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the planning, organising and controlling of the receipt, storage, issue and records of goods in a store
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: prevents loss and theft; ensures stock is available when needed; reduces waste and deterioration; keeps accurate records; controls cost; improves customer service
5 marks: (c) any five: honesty; good record keeping; organising ability; knowledge of goods; good communication; numeracy; leadership (1 mark each)
3 marks: (d) pre-sale service: help given before buying, e.g. product demonstration, advice, free trial
2 marks: (d) after-sale service: help given after buying, e.g. delivery, installation, repairs under warranty
questions.explanation: Store management controls the receipt, storage and issue of goods. It prevents loss, ensures availability, reduces waste and controls cost. A good store manager is honest, organised and numerate. Pre-sale services (demonstrations) come before purchase; after-sale services (delivery, repairs) follow it.

questions.stem:
The following information relates to item X in the store of Ade Enterprises:
Maximum usage 400 units per week; minimum usage 150 units per week; average usage 250 units per week; maximum lead time 5 weeks; minimum lead time 2 weeks; average lead time 3 weeks; reorder quantity 2,500 units.
(a) Calculate: (i) the reorder level; (ii) the maximum stock level; (iii) the minimum stock level. [12 marks]
(b) Explain the difference between periodic stock taking and perpetual inventory. [4 marks]
(c) State two advantages of a computerised stock control system. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a)(i) reorder level = 400 x 5 = 2,000 units
4 marks: (a)(ii) maximum level = 2,000 + 2,500 - (150 x 2) = 4,200 units
4 marks: (a)(iii) minimum level = 2,000 - (250 x 3) = 1,250 units
2 marks: (b) periodic: stock is physically counted at fixed intervals
2 marks: (b) perpetual: records are updated after every receipt and issue, giving a continuous balance
4 marks: (c) any two, 2 marks each: faster and accurate records; automatic reorder alerts; easy reports; reduced paperwork; real-time stock information
questions.explanation: Reorder level = 400 x 5 = 2,000. Maximum level = 2,000 + 2,500 - 300 = 4,200. Minimum level = 2,000 - 750 = 1,250. Periodic stock taking counts at intervals; perpetual inventory updates continuously. Computers speed up records and give automatic reorder alerts.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of government regulation of business. [2 marks]
(b) State three roles each of: (i) NAFDAC; (ii) SON; (iii) NDLEA. [12 marks]
(c) Explain the meaning of: (i) trade mark; (ii) copyright; (iii) licence. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the control of business activities by government through laws, agencies and licences to protect consumers, workers and the public
4 marks: (b)(i) NAFDAC: any two of registering food and drugs; inspecting factories; controlling fake drugs; regulating labelling and advertising (2 marks each)
4 marks: (b)(ii) SON: any two of setting product standards; testing and certifying products; preventing substandard imports; inspecting factories (2 marks each)
4 marks: (b)(iii) NDLEA: any two of preventing drug trafficking; arresting and prosecuting offenders; destroying illicit drugs; public enlightenment on drug abuse (2 marks each)
2 marks: (c)(i) trade mark: a registered name, symbol or design that identifies a firm's goods
2 marks: (c)(ii) copyright: exclusive legal right of an author or creator over the use of an original work
2 marks: (c)(iii) licence: an official permit to carry on a particular business or activity
questions.explanation: Government regulates business to protect the public. NAFDAC registers and controls food and drugs; SON sets and enforces product standards; NDLEA fights illicit drugs. A trade mark identifies goods; copyright protects creative works; a licence permits an activity.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between home trade documents and foreign trade documents. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the use of each of the following documents: (i) enquiry; (ii) pro-forma invoice; (iii) consignment note; (iv) certificate of origin; (v) letter of credit; (vi) consular invoice. [18 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) home trade documents are used in buying and selling within a country; foreign trade documents are used in importing and exporting
3 marks: (b)(i) enquiry: sent by a buyer to a seller asking for prices, terms and availability of goods
3 marks: (b)(ii) pro-forma invoice: an advance invoice sent before goods, for prepayment, quotation or customs purposes
3 marks: (b)(iii) consignment note: accompanies goods sent by road/rail, giving details of goods and consignee
3 marks: (b)(iv) certificate of origin: states the country where the goods were produced, for customs duty and trade agreements
3 marks: (b)(v) letter of credit: issued by the importer's bank guaranteeing payment to the exporter on presentation of documents
3 marks: (b)(vi) consular invoice: signed by the consul of the importing country, confirming the value and origin of goods
questions.explanation: Home trade documents are used within a country; foreign trade documents in international trade. An enquiry asks for terms; a pro-forma invoice comes before goods; a consignment note accompanies goods; a certificate of origin shows where goods were made; a letter of credit guarantees payment; a consular invoice is certified by the importing country's consul.

questions.stem:
The following balances were taken from the books of Iyabo Stores for the year ended 31 December:
Sales ₦850,000; Purchases ₦520,000; Opening stock ₦70,000; Closing stock ₦90,000; Rent ₦48,000; Wages ₦72,000; Electricity ₦18,000.
(a) Prepare the Trading and Profit and Loss Account for the year. [12 marks]
(b) Calculate the rate of stock turnover. [4 marks]
(c) State two purposes of preparing final accounts. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) opening stock 70,000 + purchases 520,000 = 590,000
2 marks: (a) less closing stock 90,000; cost of sales ₦500,000
2 marks: (a) gross profit 850,000 - 500,000 = ₦350,000
3 marks: (a) expenses: rent 48,000; wages 72,000; electricity 18,000 = ₦138,000
3 marks: (a) net profit ₦212,000
2 marks: (b) average stock = (70,000 + 90,000)/2 = ₦80,000
2 marks: (b) 500,000 / 80,000 = 6.25 times
4 marks: (c) any two, 2 marks each: to find the profit or loss; to show the financial position; for tax assessment; to obtain loans; for planning and control
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = 70,000 + 520,000 - 90,000 = 500,000; GP = ₦350,000; expenses ₦138,000; NP = ₦212,000. Stock turnover = 500,000 / 80,000 = 6.25 times. Final accounts show profit and financial position and support tax and loan applications.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of investment. [2 marks]
(b) State four functions of the stock exchange. [8 marks]
(c) State three advantages of holding shares. [6 marks]
(d) Explain the following money market instruments: (i) treasury bill; (ii) commercial paper. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the use of money to acquire assets that are expected to yield income or increase in value in the future
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: provides a market for buying and selling securities; helps companies raise long-term capital; helps government raise funds; protects investors through regulation of dealings; provides information on share prices; encourages savings and investment
6 marks: (c) any three, 2 marks each: dividends; capital gains; shares can be sold easily (liquidity); voting rights; can be used as collateral; limited liability
2 marks: (d)(i) treasury bill: a short-term government security sold at a discount and redeemed at face value after a short period
2 marks: (d)(ii) commercial paper: a short-term unsecured promissory note issued by large companies to raise funds
questions.explanation: Investment uses money to acquire income-yielding assets. The stock exchange provides a market for securities, helps firms and government raise capital and protects investors. Shares give dividends, capital gains and liquidity. Treasury bills are short-term government securities; commercial papers are short-term company notes.
